title: RepoBench: Benchmarking Repository-Level Code Auto-Completion Systems
note: Full text (html): RepoBench-R benchmarks lexical (Jaccard/Edit) vs semantic (CodeBERT/UniXcoder cosine) retrieval of cross-file snippets; RepoBench-C uses 2k/8k fixed-length prompt variants but does not hold budget constant while comparing retrieval mechanisms.

title: CodeAgent: Enhancing Code Generation with Tool-Integrated Agent Systems for Real-World Repo-level Coding Challenges
note: Full text (html): agent chooses among 5 tools (web search, BM25 doc retrieval, tree-sitter symbol navigation, format checker, code interpreter) via ReAct/Tool-Planning/OpenAIFunc/Rule-based strategies; per-tool ablation (Table 5) vs NoAgent baseline, no budget matching.

title: R2C2-Coder: Enhancing and Benchmarking Real-world Repository-level Code Completion Abilities of Code Large Language Models
note: Full text (html): dual pool of tree-sitter-derived abstract/declaration context and raw 10-line snippet context, retrieved via Jaccard/BM25 up to a 4096-token cap; ablations remove abstract or snippet context and vary similarity metric without matched-budget design.

title: On the Impacts of Contexts on Repository-Level Code Generation
note: Full text (html): dependencies located via call-graph static analysis and repository graph mapping, inserted as raw code; full/medium(signature+docstring)/small(signature-only) context sizes compared but with differing avg token counts (363/253/180), not budget-matched.

title: aiXcoder-7B-v2: Training LLMs to Fully Utilize the Long Context in Repository-level Code Completion
note: Full text (html): cross-file context is raw text combining SCIP import-based dependency files and Jaccard-similarity-retrieved 20-line snippets (top-10), up to 128K tokens; ablation (Table VI) only varies training-data/pipeline stages, not context representation, and ties main gains to COLA training rather than a matched-budget comparison.

title: SWE-Debate: Competitive Multi-Agent Debate for Software Issue Resolution
note: Abstract-only (arxiv.org/abs, no html follow-up): fault propagation traces are generated by traversing a code dependency graph, then multiple agents debate over these traces; SOTA vs baselines on SWE-bench reported without budget-matching detail visible from abstract.

title: LongCodeZip: Compress Long Context for Code Language Models
note: Full text (html): two-stage compression over raw function/class-level chunks - coarse-grained perplexity-based function ranking, then fine-grained perplexity-based block selection under an adaptive budget; compared to RAG/other baselines at each method's own best compression ratio (e.g. 4.3x vs 3.1x), not a common fixed budget.

title: Repository Intelligence Graph: Deterministic Architectural Map for LLM Code Assistants
note: Abstract-only (arxiv.org/abs, quotes were substantial but no separate html fetch): SPADE deterministically extracts a build/test dependency graph (components, tests, packages, coverage edges) from CMake/CTest artifacts, exposed whole as JSON; with/without-RIG comparison (30 questions/repo) shows +12.2% accuracy, -53.9% time, no token-budget control mentioned.

title: SWE-Adept: An LLM-Based Agentic Framework for Deep Codebase Analysis and Structured Issue Resolution
note: Full text (html): per-file lightweight adjacency lists (contains/invokes edges) form a code-structure tree; the LLM agent itself performs depth-first, dependency-bounded exploration (find_child_unit) rather than a fixed algorithm; SWE-Bench Lite/Pro results are outcome comparisons (resolve rate, token counts reported separately), not budget-matched.

title: Context-as-AI-Service: Surfacing Cross-File Dependency Chains for LLM-Generated Developer Documentation
note: Full text (html): despite the title, dependency chains are surfaced indirectly - CAIS is a BM25+dense (reciprocal rank fusion) index over source/APIs/docs that the agent queries and then follows up by opening files; baseline (same repo tools minus CAIS) vs CAIS-augmented agent compared on two workflows/one SDK, isolating the retrieval layer but not matching token budget (CAIS lowers token usage).

title: What Context Does a Coding Agent Actually Need to Act?
note: Full text (html): oracle localization held fixed while representation is varied across deterministic rungs (full-body, method-only, UML-class-skeleton, signature+doc, name, exclude) on SWE-bench Verified; arms carry very different mean context sizes (25,426 vs 8,629 vs 6,876 tokens), so comparison is explicitly not budget-matched despite being a controlled ablation.

title: CodeNib: A Multi-View Data System for Serving Repository Context to Coding Agents
note: Full text (html): co-equal lexical/dense/structural(typed graph) views feed ranked retrieval (dense top-k) with optional one-hop graph expansion; policies (grep/read, eager, compact) compared across 5 models on trajectory tokens (50-87% reduction) subject to a localization-quality threshold rather than a pre-registered matched-budget design.
